extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system; computational algebraists and mathematicians using SINGULAR libraries
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in the SINGULAR computer-algebra system libraries (matrix.lib, linalg.lib, absfact.lib, algebra.lib): usages, assumptions, return values, notes, and examples for each procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: symmetricBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from library matrix.lib producing a polynomial ring and an ideal 'symBasis' that is a basis of the k-th symmetric power of an n-dimensional vector space. The output polynomial ring has characteristic 0 and n variables named by the chosen base name (optional string argument) or 'e' by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes/examples: Example shows symmetricBasis(4,3,"@e") producing a container ring with QQ coefficients and 4 variables and symBasis[1..20] giving monomials like @e(4)^3, @e(3)*@e(4)^2, ..., @e(1)^3. See Section D.3.1.30 [exteriorBasis] for related functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: exteriorBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from library matrix.lib returning a qring (exterior algebra) containing the ideal 'extBasis' which is a basis of the k-th exterior power of an n-dimensional vector space. The output ring has characteristic 0 and n variables named by the optional base name (default 'e').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes/examples: Example: exteriorBasis(4,3,"@e") shows noncommutative relations (anti-commutation) like @e(2)@e(1) = -@e(1)*@e(2) and extBasis entries like @e(2)*@e(3)*@e(4), etc. See also symmetricBasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: symmetricPower
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: symmetricPower(A, k); where A is a module and k an integer. Return: module equal to the k-th symmetric power of A. Chosen bases and intermediate data are shown if printlevel is large enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes/examples: Works over commutative K-algebras and exterior algebras (example shows differing outputs and zero results over exterior algebra). Example demonstrates print(symmetricPower(B,2)) and print(symmetricPower(B,3)) with explicit monomial lists. See also exteriorPower.

rubrics_metrics.name: exteriorPower
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: exteriorPower(A, k); A a module, k integer. Return: module representing the k-th exterior power of A. Note that chosen bases and intermediate data may be displayed depending on printlevel; last rows invisible if zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes/examples: Examples show outputs for various modules; when used over superCommutative() ring (exterior algebra) quotient relations like a2,b2,... set to zero and results computed accordingly. See symmetricPower for contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: inverse
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from linalg.lib. Usage: inverse(A [,opt]); A a square matrix, opt integer. Return: the inverse matrix of A if invertible, or the 1x1 0-matrix if A is not invertible (in the polynomial ring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: opt=0 (or not given) choose heuristically; opt=1 apply std to (transpose(E,A)), ordering (C,dp); opt=2 apply interred (transpose(E,A)), ordering (C,dp) (only correct for matrices with entries in a field); opt=3 apply lift(A,E), ordering (C,dp). Examples provided illustrating usage and outputs. See inverse_B and inverse_L for alternate behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: inverse_B
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: inverse_B(A); A square matrix. Return: list Inv with Inv[1] = matrix I and Inv[2] = poly p such that I*A = unitmat(n)*p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: p=1 if 1/det(A) is computable, otherwise p=det(A). Computation uses busadj. Example shows Inv[1], Inv[2] and Inv[1]*A equals scalar polynomial times identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: inverse_L
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: inverse_L(A); A square matrix. Return: list Inv representing a left inverse of A (Inv[1] = matrix I and Inv[2] = poly p such that I*A = unitmat(n)*p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: p=1 if 1/det(A) is computable, otherwise p=det(A). The computation first computes det(A) and then uses lift. Example shows returned Inv and verification Inv[1]*A.

rubrics_metrics.name: sym_gauss
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sym_gauss(A); A symmetric matrix. Return: matrix, the diagonalisation of A using the symmetric Gauss algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: sym_gauss on [[1,4],[4,15]] returns [[1,0],[0,-1]].

rubrics_metrics.name: orthogonalize
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: orthogonalize(A); A is a matrix of constants. Return: matrix giving an orthogonal basis of the column space of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: orthogonalize applied to a 4x4 numeric matrix yields a diagonal matrix with orthogonal basis (example shows eigen-like diagonal output).

rubrics_metrics.name: diag_test
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: diag_test(A); A a constant square matrix. Return: int 1 if A is diagonalizable, 0 if not, -1 if no statement possible because A does not split.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Test works only for split matrices (eigenvalues in ground field). Does not work with parameters (uses factorize,gcd). Example returns 1 for a given matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: busadj
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: busadj(A); A square matrix of size n. Return: list L where L[1] contains the (n+1) coefficients of the characteristic polynomial and L[2] contains the n nxn matrices Hk that are coefficients of the busadjoint bA = adjoint(E*t - A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates building the polynomial X from L[1] and forming bA from L[2], and verifying bA*(t*unitmat - A) equals characteristic polynomial times identity. Useful as backend for adjoint/determinant computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: charpoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: charpoly(A[,v]); A square matrix, v optional variable name. Return: poly the characteristic polynomial det(E*v - A) (default variable is name of last variable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: A must be independent of v. Computation uses det. If printlevel>0, recursive display of det(E*v-A) occurs. Example shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: adjoint
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: adjoint(A); A square matrix. Return: adjoint matrix of A, satisfying Adj*A = det(A)*E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: computation uses busadj(A). Example demonstrates Adj*A equals determinant times identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: det_B
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: det_B(A); A any matrix. Return: determinant of A computed via the busadj algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: det_B on a 10x10 matrix returns a polynomial of degree 10; the procedure uses busadj internally.

rubrics_metrics.name: gaussred
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gaussred(A); A any constant matrix. Return: list Z where Z[1]=P, Z[2]=U, Z[3]=S, Z[4]=rank(A), giving a row-reduced matrix S, permutation matrix P and normalized lower triangular U with P*A = U*S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Designed for teaching; implementation is not very efficient. Example shows P, U, S and rank, with verification P*A and U*S.

rubrics_metrics.name: gaussred_pivot
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gaussred_pivot(A); A any constant matrix. Return: same as gaussred but with row pivoting: list Z with Z[1]=P, Z[2]=U, Z[3]=S, Z[4]=rank(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: behaves like gaussred but performs row pivoting. Example demonstrates outputs and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: gauss_nf
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gauss_nf(A); A any constant matrix. Return: matrix; the Gauss normal form of A (uses gaussred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: gauss_nf on a 4x4 matrix returns an upper-triangular-like normal form with one nonzero diagonal block entries and zeros elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: mat_rk
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: mat_rk(A); A any constant matrix. Return: int, the rank of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example returns rank 3 for a given 4x4 matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: U_D_O
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: U_D_O(A); A constant invertible matrix. Return: list Z with Z[1]=P (permutation), Z[2]=U (normalized lower triangular), Z[3]=D (diagonal), Z[4]=O (normalized upper triangular) such that P*A = U*D*O.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Z[1] = -1 indicates A is not regular (proc uses gaussred). Example prints P,U,D,O and verifies product equals P*A.

rubrics_metrics.name: pos_def
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: pos_def(A); A constant symmetric square matrix. Return: int 1 if A is positive definite, 0 if not, -1 if unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: pos_def returns 0 and 1 on example matrices. Assumes constant symmetric inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: hessenberg
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: hessenberg(M); M a constant square matrix. Return: matrix H, the Hessenberg form of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume M is constant. Example shows that an already upper Hessenberg matrix returns unchanged. See also system.

rubrics_metrics.name: eigenvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: eigenvals(M); M a matrix. Assume eigenvalues of M lie in the basefield. Return: list l where l[1] is an ideal of eigenvalues and l[2] an intvec of multiplicities (l[2][i] multiplicity of l[1][i]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Assumes eigenvalues in base field. Example shows outputs for a triangular matrix. See also procedures related to Jordan normal form.

rubrics_metrics.name: minipoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minipoly(M); M a matrix. Assume eigenvalues of M lie in the basefield. Return: list l giving the minimal polynomial of M as an ideal and multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: same assumption as eigenvals. Example shows returned minimal polynomial roots and multiplicities.

rubrics_metrics.name: spnf
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spnf(list(a[,m])); a is an ideal, m an intvec. Assume ncols(a) == size(m). Return: list l where l[1] is ideal of generators (sorted unique) and l[2] is intvec of multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: spnf prints a compact spectrum representation like (-1/2,1),(-3/10,2),...; helper routine spprint displays spectrum.

rubrics_metrics.name: spprint
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spprint(sp); sp a list (helper for spnf). Return: string s representing the spectrum sp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates formatted output of spectrum pairs. See spnf for usage context.

rubrics_metrics.name: jordan
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: jordan(M); M a matrix. Assume eigenvalues of M lie in the basefield. Return: list l with Jordan data: l[1] ideal of eigenvalues (one per Jordan block), l[2] intvec of sizes of Jordan blocks, l[3] intvec of multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates typical output giving Jordan block eigenvalues and sizes. Many Jordan-related helpers are provided (jordanbasis, jordanmatrix, jordannf).

rubrics_metrics.name: jordanbasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: jordanbasis(M); M matrix. Assume eigenvalues in basefield. Return: list l where l[1] is a module (basis) and l[2] an intvec weight filtration; inverse(l[1])*M*l[1] is in Jordan normal form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example prints basis matrix l[1], weight indices l[2], and verifies transformed matrix is Jordan normal form.

rubrics_metrics.name: jordanmatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: jordanmatrix(list(e,s,m)); e ideal, s intvec sizes, m intvec multiplicities. Assume ncols(e) == size(s) == size(m). Return: matrix J, the Jordan matrix with given block eigenvalues/sizes/multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs a Jordan matrix from e=(2,3), s=(1,2), m=(1,1) and prints 3x3 Jordan matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: jordannf
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: jordannf(M); M matrix. Assume eigenvalues in basefield. Return: matrix J, the Jordan normal form of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: jordannf on a 3x3 matrix returns a block-diagonal Jordan form matching jordan and jordanbasis outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: absFactorize
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from absfact.lib. Usage: absFactorize(p [,s]); p a polynomial, optional s string naming new parameter. Assume coefficient field Q or transcendental extension over Q. Return: ring R (current basering + new parameter) and a list absolute_factors with entries describing absolute factorization: absolute_factors[1] ideals (factors), [2] intvec multiplicities, [3] ideals (minimal polynomials for field extensions), [4] total number of nontrivial absolute factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: All factors are presented denominator- and content-free. The constant factor is chosen so product of absolute factors equals p / constant. Example demonstrates creating a new ring S and accessing absolute_factors. See absFactorizeBCG for alternate algorithm (Bertone-Cheze-Galligo).

rubrics_metrics.name: absFactorizeBCG
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: absFactorizeBCG(p [,s]); p poly, optional s string. Assume coefficient field Q or transcendental extension. Return: ring R augmented by parameter and absolute_factors list analogous to absFactorize (absolute factors, multiplicities, minimal polynomials, count).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Uses algorithm of Bertone, Cheze and Galligo for bivariate reduction and similar lifting; output format same as absFactorize. Example shows returned absolute_factors and minimal polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: algebra_containment
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from algebra.lib. Usage: algebra_containment(p,A[,k]); p poly, A ideal whose generators A[1]..A[m] generate a subalgebra. Return: if k=0 (default) integer 1 if p in K[A], 0 otherwise; if k=1 return list l with l[1] = 1/0 and l[2] a ring containing a polynomial check describing the relation p = h(A[...]) or the nonlinear relation if not contained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Algorithm introduces new variables y(i) and uses product order x(i) >> y(i); p reduces to polynomial only in y(i) iff p in subalgebra. The proc inSubring uses a different (sometimes faster) algorithm. Example shows usage and how to access the ring and check polynomial created.

rubrics_metrics.name: module_containment
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from algebra.lib. Usage: module_containment(p,P,M[,k]); P = generators of a subalgebra, M = generators of a module over K[P]. Assume ncols(P)=nvars(basering) and P[i] algebraically independent. Return: if k=0 integer 1 if p in module <M> over K[P], 0 otherwise; if k=1 return list l with l[1] and l[2] ring containing polynomial check describing representation or relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Introduces new variables y(j), z(i) and product order; p reduces to polynomial only in y,z and linear in z iff p in module. Example shows returned ring and checks; when l[1]=0 the ring contains a polynomial relation accessible by naming the ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: inSubring
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from algebra.lib. Usage: inSubring(p,i); p poly, i ideal with generators i[1]..i[k]. Return: list l with l[1] integer and l[2] string: l[1]=1 iff p is in subring generated by i (then l[2] = y(0)-h(y(1),...,y(k)) with p = h(i[...])), l[1]=0 iff not (l[2] contains relation h(y(0),y(1),...,y(k)) satisfied by p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: algebra_containment tests same relation with a different algorithm. If l[1]==0, l[2] may contain multiple relations separated by commas. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: algDependent
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from algebra.lib. Usage: algDependent(f[,c]); f an ideal f1..fm, c an integer selecting algorithm. Return: list l of size 2 where l[1]=1 if f1..fm are algebraically dependent (0 otherwise), and l[2] a ring containing ideal 'ker' describing algebraic relations between the f[i] (kernel of map K[y1..ym] -> basering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Three algorithms depending on c (1,2,3); if c omitted heuristic choice. Basering may be a quotient ring. To access ker, assign l[2] to a name and setring. Example shows returned ker and substituted relations. Displayed commentary depends on printlevel.

rubrics_metrics.name: alg_kernel
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: alg_kernel(phi,pr[,s,c]); phi map to basering, pr preimage ring, optional s string name for kernel, c integer algorithm selector. Return: string giving the kernel of phi as a string; if s given, creates kernel named s in preimage ring pr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Three algorithm variants depending on c; if c omitted heuristic used. Kernel lives in preimage ring so cannot be returned to basering unless named. Basering may be a quotient ring. Example usage outline provided.
